references.text: The description of the priestly garments that Aaron and his sons were to wear, including the linen tunic, sash, and turban, which are the same items mentioned in Leviticus 16:4.
The making of the linen tunic, turban, and undergarments from fine twisted linen for Aaron and his sons.
The command that Aaron and his sons must wash with water before serving, as also required in Leviticus 16:4.
Moses is instructed to bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tabernacle, wash them with water, and then clothe Aaron in the holy garments.
The priest shall put on the linen tunic and linen undergarments when performing his service at the altar.
Ezekiel's vision concerning priests who must wear linen garments while serving in the inner court, and nothing made of wool.
The bride's pure and shining linen garments symbolize the righteous acts of the saints, pointing back to the holy linen garments worn by the priest.
The high priest enters the Most Holy Place once a year, not without blood, referring to Aaron's service on the Day of Atonement described in Leviticus 16.
